item.title: Has Trump struck more countries than any modern president?
item.description: Sen. Elizabeth Warren says President Donald Trump has targeted more countries than any other 21st century president. Is that accurate?

item.title: Did Iran pose an imminent threat to the US? Who decides?
item.description: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard told senators it’s the president’s responsibility, and not that of the intelligence community, to determine what threats against the U.S. are imminent. Experts say that’s part of the intelligence community’s job.

item.title: Need an ID to shovel snow in NYC? To get hired and paid, yes
item.description: Republicans defending voter ID rules in the SAVE America Act say you need an ID to shovel snow in New York City. But that’s only if you are hired to shovel. Federal law requires identification to get paid.

item.title: Do 1 in 10 Americans lack ID needed under SAVE America Act?
item.description: Democrats opposing the SAVE America Act, which would require certain documents to register to vote and cast a ballot, point to a study showing 9% of adult U.S. citizens would have difficulty with those requirements.

item.title: Fact-checking James Fishback on youth underemployment
item.description: Florida Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback said 70% of young, U.S. college grads are underemployed. That's False. Data shows the current rate is about 42% and has ranged from 38% to 48% since 2008.

item.title: How Iran conducts influence operations
item.description: The Trump administration warned of Iran’s wartime disinformation. Iran has been building its broader influence operation capabilities for more than a decade. Here’s how the regime attempts to manipulate public opinion and control narratives.

item.title: Could TSA agents be paid with passengers’ ticket fees?
item.description: Some social media users are encouraging the use of passengers’ ticket fees to pay TSA agents during the government shutdown. But that’s not possible under current federal law.

item.title: Sports betting: Casual entertainment or cause for concern?
item.description: As March Madness ramps up, you’re likely to see ads for sports betting apps and websites. Here’s how to recognize signs when gambling is cause for concern and how to lend support.

item.title: This video does not show Israelis fleeing to Cyprus
item.description: This video of people rushing to get on a boat does not show Israelis recently trying to escape to Cyprus. It’s from the Philippines.

item.title: Partial government shutdown: Why does ICE get paid, not TSA?
item.description: Trump deployed ICE agents to certain U.S. airports to support TSA agents amid a partial government shutdown that has left Homeland Security without funding. Both ICE and TSA are part of the DHS, but only ICE agents are getting paid. Here’s why.

item.title: Would SAVE America Act require you to reregister to vote?
item.description: The SAVE America Act would not require everyone to reregister to vote. But if it passes the Senate, it would affect millions of people who register for the first time or change their registration.

item.title: Did activists cause power outage and patient deaths in Cuba?
item.description: A group of liberal activists visited Cuba to deliver aid amid a deepening humanitarian crisis. Did they stay in five-star hotels? Did they have to? Did an activist concert lead to Cuban deaths? We fact-checked these claims.

item.title: Facts on the vitamin K shot for newborns
item.description: Your first memory of vitamins may involve Flintstones chewables. But if you were born after 1961, a doctor probably gave you vitamin K shortly after birth. For decades, U.S. health officials have recommended the shot to prevent dangerous internal bleeding in babies.
